dedupe_keys.name: infrastructure climate resilience assessment data starter kits per country zenodo

description: The Data Starter Kits are national extracts of global open datasets on climate hazards and infrastructure, one kit per country (or part of a country), clipped with Natural Earth boundaries, meant as a starting point for climate risk analysis where data are scattered or hard to use, especially in low- and middle-income countries. Each kit gathers hazards (coastal and river flooding, extreme heat and drought, tropical cyclone wind speeds), exposure (population and built-up area from GHSL, OpenStreetMap roads and railways, power plants and power transmission lines) and context (elevation, land use and land cover, geoBoundaries administrative units), so that hazard and exposure can be intersected as a first step to vulnerability and risk. They are made by Tom Russell, Diana Jaramillo, Chris Nicholas, Fred Thomas, Raghav Pant and Jim W. Hall at the University of Oxford and published in the Climate Compatible Growth community on Zenodo; the Sudan kit, version 0.2.1 of 28 July 2025, is one zip file of about 600 MB, and the kits handed to this piece cover 110 countries. They are accessible as free downloads under CC BY-SA 4.0 and point to the snkit, nismod-snail and open-gira Python tools. Caveats: global inputs clipped to countries carry their original resolution and errors, and the boundaries express no view on sovereignty. They support hazard exposure and infrastructure risk simulation across transport and energy networks; related records are open-gira, SNAIL and GIRI.
